title: All Hail, Life-bearing Cross
description: All Hail, Life-bearing Cross in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Greek Office Books (Paisley, 1904), headed “Stichera”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre (6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: All hail, life bear-ing Cross, The tro-phy of the good, Thy bloom is fra-grance on our way, Thy fruit our heav-enly food.

lines: Thy bloom is fragrance on our way,
The Church's fortress when the foe
By thee the curse is gone,
We cast his power beneath our feet,
And foe of all our foes;
The glory of the saints of God,
Their crown for all their woes.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Greek Office Books (1904)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Greek Office Books; set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
